subject: botany
intro: Botany is plant science from the cell to the biome, and it leads to work growing food, mapping soils, protecting ecosystems and teaching the green world.

roles.title: Soil and Plant Scientists
roles.what: Research the breeding, physiology, yield and management of crops and other plants, and the chemical, physical and biological composition of soils as they relate to plant growth — sometimes classifying and mapping soils.
roles.where: Plant tissues and organs, photosynthesis including C4 and CAM pathways, water potential and transport, and the genetics-and-breeding unit give you exactly the crop-and-soil research toolkit.

roles.title: Conservation Scientists
roles.what: Manage, improve and protect natural resources, conducting soil surveys and developing plans to eliminate soil erosion or protect rangelands, and advising farmers and ranchers on rotation and land care.
roles.where: The plant-ecology unit — succession, biomes of the world, invasive plants — and economic botany's conservation-of-diversity strand feed directly into land-management advice and erosion planning.

roles.title: Agricultural Technicians
roles.what: Work with agricultural scientists on plant research: maintain laboratory equipment, collect crop samples, prepare specimens and record data, running tests that improve yield, quality and resistance to disease and insects.
roles.where: Plant breeding and genetic modification from unit 7, the tissue systems of unit 3, and the physiological measurement of water relations are the sampling, testing and recording skills the role is built on.

roles.title: Agricultural Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in the agricultural sciences, including agronomy and horticultural sciences, combining classroom and laboratory teaching with research on crops, soils and cropping systems.
roles.where: The syllabus's arc from plant cell to economic botany maps onto agronomy and horticulture curricula, and the ethnobotany unit's centres-of-crop-origin topic is a classic lecture of its own.
